title: Landing page or website: which one sells more?
excerpt: Learn when to choose a landing page and when to choose a website, with cost, conversion, and SEO criteria to decide which format sells more for your business.
content:
Choosing between a landing page or a website depends on your goal: if you want to sell a product or service or capture leads from a specific campaign, a landing page usually converts better; if the goal is online presence, authority, and organic traffic from Google, a full website is the right path. In the view of OutBox Soluções Digitais, many businesses actually need both formats.

In Santa Cruz do Rio Pardo and all over Brazil, this question comes up a lot among people starting a business or launching a new offer. The good news is that the decision gets simple once you compare the two with clear criteria, like cost, timeline, conversion goal, and long-term strategy.

What's the difference between a landing page and a website?

A landing page (or LP) is a single page built for one specific goal: selling a product, capturing contacts, or getting sign-ups. It has little or no navigation to other pages, because every extra link is a chance for the visitor to get distracted and leave without acting.

A website is a set of connected pages: about, services, blog, contact. It works as the company's online headquarters, serving different audiences and interests at the same time. People who arrive from Google can browse, get to know the company, compare solutions, and decide with more information.

In short:

  • Landing page: focused on 1 goal, 1 audience, and 1 action (buy, download, book, request a quote).
  • Website: the brand's full presence, with several pages covering many different search intents.

When is a landing page the right choice?

A landing page works best when you have a clear offer and a specific audience. It removes distractions and takes visitors straight to the action. It works well in these cases:

  • Launching a new product or service.
  • Paid ad campaigns on Google or social media.
  • Lead capture: e-book, quote, booking, waitlist.
  • Promotions and seasonal dates (Black Friday, school enrollment, registrations).
  • Offers from local businesses, like clinics, law offices, schools, and construction services that need a quick response.

A practical example: a clinic advertising evaluation appointments doesn't want the ad click to land on the website's home page, where people find 15 other pieces of information. An LP with the offer, proof of credibility, a short form, and a WhatsApp button tends to generate more contacts for the same ad spend.

The reason is simple: fewer options, more focus. That's why a good landing page works with 1 promise, 1 call to action, and the fewest form fields needed to qualify the contact.

When is a full website worth more?

A full website is the best choice when the goal is to build a long-term online presence. It covers a wide range of searches, supports the brand's authority, and keeps feeding the funnel without relying only on ads.

  • Companies that sell more than 1 solution and need to explain each one in detail.
  • Businesses that depend on Google to be found organically, without paying per click.
  • Industries where customers research a lot before deciding: law, healthcare, manufacturing, education, technology.
  • Companies that need a blog to attract visitors and educate their audience.

The blog deserves a special mention here. Every article optimized for a specific search is a permanent way into the website. While an ad campaign stops when the budget runs out, well-ranked content keeps bringing in visitors for months. That's what we call an SEO strategy: working on the website so it shows up in search without depending on paid media.

For businesses that serve clients in different regions of Brazil, as OutBox Soluções Digitais does, the website is also where the service pages, social proof, and contact channels live, giving confidence to people who are just getting to know the company.

Does a landing page convert better than a website?

In single-goal campaigns, a landing page usually converts better, precisely because it removes navigation and distractions. Data from the Brazilian market helps put the comparison in perspective: according to Leadster's 2025 Lead Generation Report, the median conversion rate for websites in Brazil is 2.98%. A well-built LP, focused on 1 offer and 1 audience, usually lands above that average, because it doesn't ask visitors to "figure it out" across dozens of pages.

But keep in mind: a higher conversion rate doesn't mean better results in every scenario. An LP only works well when qualified traffic is reaching it, whether from ads, email, or posts. Without traffic sources, even the best page in the world won't sell on its own.

A website plays a different role: it captures demand that already exists on Google. Someone searches for "employment lawyer near me" and finds the service page. That search would never go through a campaign LP.

How much does each format cost and how long does it take?

Prices and timelines vary with the scope, the number of sections, and the features (forms, integrations, copy, visual identity). Generally speaking, a landing page is smaller and faster to produce, because it's 1 page with a defined goal. A full website involves more pages, more content, and more structure, which naturally increases the investment and the timeline.

Before getting a quote for either one, it's worth gathering this information:

  • Main goal: sell now or be found in the long run?
  • Do you already have copy and images, or do they need to be created?
  • Do you need a blog, WhatsApp integration, forms, or a custom system?
  • Is there a defined visual identity, or does the project include branding?

With this outline clear, the quote gets more accurate and you avoid paying for structure you won't use, or finding out later that something essential was missing.

Landing page or website: what if I need both?

For most businesses that are mature online, the answer is to use both formats together. The website supports the brand, SEO, and organic search; the landing pages receive campaign traffic with a full focus on conversion. They play complementary roles, not competing ones.

A common scenario: the business invests in content and SEO on the website to attract visitors all year, and creates a specific LP for each ad campaign or launch. That way, every real spent on media lands on a page designed to convert, while the website works on organic traffic.

How do you choose between a landing page and a website for your business?

Choose a landing page if the priority is selling 1 specific offer with paid traffic, and a website if the goal is authority, presence on Google, and steady organic traffic. When there's budget and a growth plan, both formats working together give you the best of both worlds: campaigns that convert and a website that attracts customers every day.

answer_summary: When choosing between a landing page or a website, OutBox Soluções Digitais recommends: a landing page when the goal is to sell a specific offer or capture leads in campaigns; a full website for online presence, authority, and organic traffic from Google. In practice, many businesses need both formats: the website supports the brand and the landing pages convert campaign traffic.
key_takeaways: A landing page is a single page focused on 1 goal and 1 action, ideal for campaigns and launches.
A full website covers a wide range of Google searches, supports brand authority, and works over the long term.
The median conversion rate for websites in Brazil is 2.98%, according to Leadster's 2025 Lead Generation Report.
Landing pages usually convert better in paid traffic campaigns because they remove distractions.
Without qualified traffic, a landing page won't deliver results on its own; a website captures organic demand.
A website and a landing page complement each other: one attracts, the other converts.

faq.question: Can I have just a landing page without a website?
faq.answer: You can, especially if you have a single offer and the traffic comes from ads. The problem is that an LP alone doesn't build a presence on Google or cover a range of searches. To grow with organic traffic, a full website becomes necessary at some point.

faq.question: Does a landing page show up on Google?
faq.answer: It does, but with limits. Since an LP has little content and few pages, it competes poorly in organic search. Ideally, use landing pages to receive campaign traffic and leave organic traffic to the website and the blog.

faq.question: How much does a landing page cost?
faq.answer: The price varies with the scope: number of sections, copy, images, forms, and integrations. In general, it costs less than a full website, because it's 1 page. Request a detailed quote with your goal and the features you need.

faq.question: Website or landing page for Google Ads?
faq.answer: For ads, a landing page is the default choice, because it keeps visitors focused on 1 offer and 1 action. Sending the ad click to the website's home page scatters attention and usually lowers the campaign's conversion rate.

faq.question: Is it worth having a blog on your company website?
faq.answer: Yes, when the goal is to be found organically and educate your audience. Every well-optimized article works as a permanent way in from Google, unlike ads, which stop when the budget runs out.
